name: LSD
full_name: Liquid Scintillation Detector at Mont Blanc
summary: A Soviet–Italian underground liquid-scintillator detector monitored stellar-collapse bursts and cosmic-ray particles in the Mont Blanc tunnel.
detection_principle: Scintillation counters embedded in substantial iron shielding detected prompt energy deposits and delayed neutron signatures. Low-energy burst searches looked for clustered events over seconds.

sites.name: France-Italy; underground laboratory in the Mont Blanc tunnel
sites.location: France-Italy; underground laboratory in the Mont Blanc tunnel

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The investigator review explicitly dates continuous operation January 1985–March 1999.

timeline.event: Five-event burst recorded at 02:52 UT on 23 February.

collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Scintillator target
key_parameters.value: Approximately 90 tonnes; later precise description gives 86.4 tonnes

key_parameters.name: Thresholds
key_parameters.value: Approximately 5 MeV for inner counters and 7 MeV for outer counters

results.summary: LSD’s early burst preceded the principal Kamiokande-II, IMB and Baksan signals by several hours. Its association and physical interpretation remain debated; it is not treated as equivalent confirmation of the main burst.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
